oneLiner: 专制、民主与放任——勒温用实验让孩子体验：民主组质量更高，专制组更快却更脆。
oneLinerEn: Autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire — Lewin's experiments with children: democracy gave quality, autocracy speed but fragility.
detail: 库尔特·勒温 1939 年与利皮特、怀特一起做了一项经典实验：把同一批十一岁上下的孩子分成小组做手工活动，由成年人假扮三种风格的“领导”，并在中途刻意撤走领导者观察后果。专制组效率尚可但敌意与依赖强，领导一不在场就散架；民主组更有创造力与满意度，能自我维持，领导缺席仍照常运转；放任组最散漫、产出最低且质量最差。这个“领导风格”研究第一次把民主与专制的管理差异放进实验室测量。风格并无绝对对错，勒温晚年也强调它塑造的是群体气氛与韧性；后来的路径-目标、情境领导等理论都是在这一问题上继续细化——什么时候该用哪种风格。它至今仍是领导力入门的经典坐标，也为后来的情境流派留下“风格须匹配场合”的伏笔。
detailEn: In 1939 Kurt Lewin, with Ronald Lippitt and Ralph White, ran a classic study: boys of about eleven were put into activity groups led by an adult playing one of three leadership styles, and the leader was deliberately withdrawn mid-experiment to see what happened. Autocratic groups worked acceptably but ran hot with hostility and dependency, and collapsed the moment the leader left; democratic groups were more creative and satisfied and sustained themselves with the leader absent; laissez-faire groups were the most disorganized, with the lowest output and poorest quality. It was the first time the gap between democratic and autocratic management was measured in a laboratory. No style is simply right, Lewin stressed—the style shapes the group's climate and resilience—and later path-goal and contingency theories refined the same question into "which style, when."

oneLiner: 对新手多给指令，对专家多给授权——风格要随下属的能力与意愿切换。
oneLinerEn: Direct the novice, delegate to the expert — shift style with the follower's competence and commitment.
detail: 保罗·赫塞与肯·布兰查德主张，有效的领导没有固定套路，只有四种模式沿“指令—教练—支持—授权”的光谱移动：对既无能力又缺意愿的新手先多指导，对其意愿尚存但能力不足者边指边鼓励，对有能力却信心不足者多支持少指挥，对又能干又愿担者则放手授权。判断依据是下属在特定任务上的“成熟度”（能力 + 意愿），而同一位员工在不同任务、不同阶段可能需要完全不同的对待。它直觉好用、在企业培训里传播极广，但也因四个维度难以严格验证、成熟度定义模糊而受过学理批评。尽管如此，“没有最好的风格、只有最合时宜的风格”这一常识，仍使它成为一线管理者最常被引用的入门框架之一。
detailEn: Paul Hersey and Ken Blanchard held that effective leadership has no fixed style, only four modes along an instruct-coach-support-delegate spectrum: heavy direction for the unable-and-unwilling newcomer, guidance plus encouragement for one willing but still inexperienced, high support and low direction for the capable-but-insecure, and release for those both able and willing. The dial is the subordinate's readiness on that specific task (ability plus willingness), and the same person may need sharply different treatment across tasks and stages. Intuitive and hugely popular in corporate training, it has nonetheless drawn scholarly fire because its four modes and its notion of readiness resist rigorous measurement.

oneLiner: 领导效能 = 领导风格 × 情境控制力的匹配度。
oneLinerEn: Leadership effectiveness is the match between a leader's style and the control the situation offers.
detail: 菲德勒用“最难共事同事(LPC)”量表衡量领导者是任务导向还是关系导向，再用上下级关系、任务结构、职位权力三项判断情境控制力。结论带有挑战性：任务导向者在极端有利或极端不利的处境表现更好，关系导向者在中间处境更好。而且他认为风格相对稳定，与其试图“改造人”，不如“把合适的人放到合适的岗位，或把情境改造成匹配领导”。
detailEn: Fiedler gauged whether a leader is task- or relationship-oriented with the 'Least Preferred Coworker' scale, then judged situational control from leader-member relations, task structure and position power. The conclusion was provocative: task leaders do best in situations either very favourable or very unfavourable, relationship leaders in the middle. And since he saw style as fairly fixed, he argued for matching the person to the situation — or reshaping the situation — rather than trying to rewire the person.

oneLiner: 交易型用奖惩交换绩效，变革型靠愿景、激发与关怀提升动机层次。
oneLinerEn: Transactional leaders trade rewards for performance; transformational ones raise motive through vision, stimulation and care.
detail: 伯恩斯奠基、巴斯发展：交易型领导明确“做到就给、做不到就罚”，在稳定任务中有效;变革型领导通过理想化的榜样、鼓舞人心的愿景、智力激发(鼓励质疑)与个性化关怀(因材施教)，把追随者从“为了报酬”推向“为了意义”。大量研究显示变革型与更高的绩效、承诺和满意度相关——但它需要真诚，否则易滑向作秀。
detailEn: Burns laid the groundwork, Bass developed it. Transactional leadership spells out 'deliver and be rewarded, fall short and be corrected' and works well on stable tasks. Transformational leadership uses idealised example, an inspiring vision, intellectual stimulation and individualised consideration to move followers from reward to meaning. Much research links it to higher performance, commitment and satisfaction — but it demands sincerity or it slides into theatre.

oneLiner: 生理、安全、归属、尊重、自我实现——未满足的低层需求主导行为。
oneLinerEn: Physiological, safety, belonging, esteem, self-actualisation: the lowest unsatisfied need drives behaviour.
detail: 亚伯拉罕·马斯洛 1943 年把人的需求画成一架阶梯：生理、安全、归属与爱、尊重，直至自我实现，主张低层相对满足后才向上追求（后又补上认知、审美与超越）。它对管理的启示很直接：饿着肚子或担心被裁的人，很难被“自我实现”的口号打动，薪酬与保障这些底层需求没安顿好，上层的激励就是空中楼阁。它也常被批评：实证基础薄弱、分层过于刚性、带有西方个人主义色彩，且现实中人常在穷困里照样追求创造与尊严——把它当作一个提醒而非精确模型更稳妥。不过它最大的贡献，是让“人并非只为钱工作”成为管理的主流共识，直接催生了赫茨伯格、麦格雷戈等内容型激励理论的繁荣。
detailEn: Abraham Maslow, in 1943, drew human needs as a ladder—physiological, safety, love and belonging, esteem, and self-actualization (he later added cognitive, aesthetic and transcendent needs)—holding that people pursue the higher only once the lower are relatively met. Its management lesson is direct: those who are hungry or fearing the layoff can hardly be moved by slogans of self-actualization; leave the base needs of pay and security unsettled and every higher incentive is a castle in the air. It is also much criticized—thin empirical base, tiers too rigid, tinted with Western individualism, and in real life people create and keep dignity even amid poverty—so it is best read as a prompt rather than a precise model.

oneLiner: 保健因素消除不满，激励因素带来满意——“满意”的反面不是“不满意”。
oneLinerEn: Hygiene removes dissatisfaction; motivators create satisfaction — the opposite of satisfaction is not dissatisfaction.
detail: 弗雷德里克·赫茨伯格访谈了一批会计师与工程师，问什么让工作格外满意或格外不满，得到一个反直觉的发现：薪资、公司政策、监督、工作条件这些“保健因素”不足会让人不满，但把它们做到位也只是“不再不满”，并不会真正点燃动力；真正带来满意与投入的是成就、认可、工作本身、责任与成长这些“激励因素”。满意与不满并非同一根轴的两端，而是两把独立的尺。这解释了为什么单纯加薪买不来长期敬业——它像止痛药而非维生素；要提振士气，得从工作内容与担子本身入手。后续实证对它的二分并不完全买账，但它把“别拿保健当激励”钉进了管理常识。对管理者的落点是：先消除让人不满的保健缺口，再靠丰富工作、授予责任去点燃真正的投入。
detailEn: Frederick Herzberg interviewed accountants and engineers about what made work exceptionally satisfying or intolerably dissatisfying and reached a counterintuitive result: hygiene factors—pay, company policy, supervision, working conditions—when lacking breed dissatisfaction, but perfecting them only yields the absence of dissatisfaction, never real motivation; what truly brings satisfaction and engagement are motivators—achievement, recognition, the work itself, responsibility, growth. Satisfaction and dissatisfaction, he said, are not two ends of one axis but two separate scales. This is why a bare raise cannot buy lasting engagement—it is a painkiller, not a vitamin; to lift morale you redesign the job and its stakes. Later evidence has not fully bought the split, but it fixed "do not pass off hygiene as motivation" into management common sense.

term: 麦格雷戈 X-Y 理论
oneLiner: 你假设人惰性逃避(X)还是自主负责(Y)，制度与控制风格会被这个假设自我实现。
oneLinerEn: Assume people shirk (X) or own their work (Y), and your systems make that assumption come true.
detail: 道格拉斯·麦格雷戈 (1960) 指出:持 X 假设的管理者会搭严密的监控、惩罚与集权，恰恰把人逼得消极;持 Y 假设者会给自主、参与与成长，往往激发出责任感。它是“假设会自我实现”的经典表述。后续更谨慎的 Z 理论(威廉·大内)与情境观点提醒:人不是非 X 即 Y，管理方式要看任务、文化与个人。
detailEn: Douglas McGregor (1960) argued that managers who assume Theory X build tight surveillance, punishment and centralisation — which duly makes people passive; those who assume Theory Y grant autonomy, participation and growth, and often draw out ownership. It is a classic statement that assumptions self-fulfil. Later, more careful views — Theory Z (Ouchi) and contingency — remind us people are not simply X or Y and style must fit task, culture and person.

oneLiner: 动力 = 努力能达绩效 × 绩效能得报酬 × 报酬对我有价值；任一为零，激励归零。
oneLinerEn: Motivation = expectancy × instrumentality × valence; if any term is zero, motivation collapses.
detail: 维克托·弗鲁姆 (1964) 把激励拆成三个心理判断:我相信努力能换来好绩效吗(期望)?好绩效真会换来承诺的回报吗(工具性)?那回报是我想要的吗(效价)?这条链条把“为什么画大饼没用”讲得极清楚——只要员工不信、或奖励自己压根不在乎，激励力就乘成了零。管理者的抓手，就是逐环把这三问坐实。
detailEn: Victor Vroom (1964) decomposed motivation into three beliefs: will effort yield performance (expectancy), will performance yield the promised reward (instrumentality), and is that reward something I value (valence)? It states crisply why empty promises fail — if staff disbelieve any link, or do not want the prize, the product is zero. The manager's job is to make each link real.

oneLiner: 人会把自己的“得/付出”和参照对象比；一旦觉得亏待，就想办法把它扳平。
oneLinerEn: People compare their outcomes-to-inputs with a referent; feel shortchanged and they act to restore balance.
detail: 斯塔西·亚当斯认为公平是主观感知:你算出自己的“产出 ÷ 投入”，再与同事或同行比较，若感到被亏待，就会设法恢复平衡——少干活、要求加薪、在心里换一个参照对象，或者干脆离开。它对管理的启示是:绝对数额常常不如“相对公平感”重要;因此薪酬透明与程序公正(怎么决定的、可不可申诉)格外关键。
detailEn: J. Stacy Adams held that equity is a perception: you compute your outcomes over inputs, compare it with a colleague or market referent, and — feeling under-rewarded — act to restore balance: slack off, demand more, quietly switch referents, or leave. The lesson for managers is that relative fairness often matters more than absolute pay, so pay transparency and procedural justice (how a decision was made and can it be appealed) are crucial.

oneLiner: 具体而有挑战性、并配反馈的目标，比“尽力就好”更能提升绩效。
oneLinerEn: Specific, challenging goals with feedback beat 'do your best' at driving performance.
detail: 埃德温·洛克(与莱瑟姆)经过大量研究确立:目标通过四条途径起作用——引导注意、调动努力、延长坚持、激发策略探索。前提是员工接受了目标(承诺)、并有能力与反馈支撑。它也有阴暗面:为达成一个醒目数字而牺牲质量、走捷径甚至造假——所以目标要成组(兼顾质量与长期)，并把过程诚信与心理安全感一起设计进去。
detailEn: Edwin Locke (with Latham), across hundreds of studies, established that specific, challenging goals raise performance by directing attention, mobilising effort, sustaining persistence and sparking strategy — provided the person accepts the goal and has the ability and feedback to pursue it. It has a dark side: a lone salient number invites cut corners, quality damage or outright gaming. Hence goals should come in balanced sets, with process integrity and psychological safety designed alongside.

oneLiner: 领导的本职是扫清通往目标的障碍，风格要补下属所缺(指导、支持、参与、成就导向)。
oneLinerEn: The leader's job is to clear the path to goals, choosing a style — directive, supportive, participative, achievement-oriented — that supplies what the subordinate lacks.
detail: 罗伯特·豪斯 1971 年提出的路径-目标理论，把弗鲁姆的期望理论与领导行为研究拼在一处：领导者的活儿是在下属与其目标之间搭桥，帮他们看清路径、移开路障，并根据其能力与任务结构补足缺失的一环——任务模糊就多指导，任务压抑、风险高就多支持。它列了指导型、支持型、参与型、成就导向型四种领导行为，都同一个判断标准：此刻这位下属缺什么。它把“哪种风格最好”这个老问题改写成“在什么情境对什么人用什么风格”，是权变思路的精细化版本；后续修订（如引入规范模型）又提醒它并非万能，对结构化任务过多的指挥反而多余。后续实证也坦承它对高结构、高能力下属增益有限，过度指导反成干扰——这恰是它强调“补足缺失一环”的用意。
detailEn: Robert House's path-goal theory (1971) joined Vroom's expectancy model with leadership-behavior research: the leader's job is to build a bridge between a subordinate and the goal, clarifying the path, removing obstacles, and supplying whatever is missing given the person's ability and the task's structure—more direction when the task is ambiguous, more support when it is oppressive and risky. It names four leader behaviors—directive, supportive, participative, achievement-oriented—judged by one test: what this subordinate lacks right now. It recast the old "which style is best" into "which style, for whom, in what situation," a fine-grained contingency move; later revisions (adding a normative model) warned it is no cure-all—over-directing an already-structured task only backfires.

oneLiner: 领导者与每个下属各建一段关系，有人进“圈内”、有人留在“圈外”，质量决定资源与信任。
oneLinerEn: A leader builds a separate relationship with each subordinate — an in-group and an out-group — whose quality drives trust, latitude and reward.
detail: 格雷恩与比尔（1975）从一次访谈里发现：领导并不对下属一视同仁，而是与少数人逐步发展出高质量交换——互信、额外机会、真实影响力与更包容的犯错空间（“圈内”），而多数人维持低质量的契约式关系（“圈外”：正式职权对完成分内事）。后续研究给出的关联相当稳定：圈内绩效更高、满意度与留任更强、冲突更少，而圈外成员对公平最敏感。它既解释了“嫡系”现象，也把风险说得很直：若分圈依据是贡献与可靠性，它是一套高效的人才配置；若是喜好、同校、同乡或“谁应答快”，则公平感与心理安全会被侵蚀，而且圈外人会用低投入回敬。实用启示有两层：先自查自己的圈内名单能否用事实解释（能不能说出对方具体做成过什么）；再看能否把机会与信息共享逐步往外推，因为“入圈”往往始于一次主动而非领导的选择。
detailEn: Graen and Uhl-Bien, building on 1970s fieldwork, found that leaders do not treat subordinates alike: with a few they develop high-quality exchange over time — real trust, extra opportunity, genuine influence, tolerance for well-meant errors (the in-group) — while most stay in a low-quality contractual relationship (the out-group: formal authority in exchange for the job as written). The downstream correlations are fairly stable: the in-group performs better, is more satisfied, stays longer, argues less, while out-group members are the most sensitive to fairness. The theory both explains favouritism and names its hazard. If membership tracks contribution and reliability, it is an efficient allocation of talent; if it tracks liking, alumni ties, shared hometown or who replies fastest, then fairness and psychological safety erode, and outsiders typically answer with withdrawal. Two practical implications: audit your own in-group list against facts you could state aloud (what exactly did this person deliver?), and push information and opportunity outward deliberately — since entering the in-group usually begins with someone's unprompted initiative, not with the leader's choice.

oneLiner: 领导首先是服务者——先满足下属成长与自主，权力自下而上地授予。
oneLinerEn: The leader is first a server — putting subordinates' growth and autonomy first, so authority is granted from below.
detail: 罗伯特·格林利夫 1970 年在《仆人式领导》里倒转了权力的方向：真正的领导者先是仆人——先问“团队需要什么”而非“我要他们做什么”，通过倾听、共情、觉察、说服、管家责任与致力于他人成长来赋能，而不是靠职位发号施令。他提醒：判断一个领导是否真在“服务”，可看被服务的人是否更健康、自主、更有能力也把自己变成仆人。它把变革型的“提升动机”再推进一步——把目的从组织绩效部分转向人的成长，成为后来谦逊领导、倒金字塔与赋能管理的源头。也有批评说它过于理想化、在需要当机立断的危机里未必顶用。它也常被追问“服务”与“软弱”的界线在哪——答案或许是，服务他人并不等于放弃决断，而是把决断用在如何服务于人上。
detailEn: Robert Greenleaf reversed the direction of power in The Servant as Leader (1970): the genuine leader is a servant first—asking "what does the team need" rather than "what will they do for me," empowering through listening, empathy, awareness, persuasion, stewardship and a commitment to others' growth instead of commanding from a title. His test for whether a leader truly serves: do the served people grow healthier, wiser, more autonomous, and more likely to become servants themselves? It pushes transformational leadership a step further—shifting the aim from organizational performance partly toward human growth—and became the wellspring of humble, inverted-pyramid and empowering management. Critics call it idealized, not always decisive in a crisis demanding instant command.

term: 管理 4C（清晰·承诺·能力·控制）
oneLiner: 让事情真正发生靠四环：把目标说清晰、拿到真承诺、配得上能力、留得住控制。
oneLinerEn: Getting things done holds on four Cs — Clarity of goal, genuine Commitment, matching Competence and steady Control.
detail: 一条把“管理”落到执行闭环的清单：Clarity 让每个成员对目标与标准有清晰一致的理解，别靠猜；Commitment 是被真正认可而非口头答应的投入，靠参与而非强压；Competence 是把合适的人放在合适的事上并补齐能力缺口；Control 不是微观插手，而是建立可见的进度与纠偏机制，跑偏时及时发现。四者缺一，计划就停在纸面；它常用来诊断“为什么定好的事执行不下去”。
detailEn: A checklist that turns management into an execution loop: Clarity means every member shares a clear, aligned read of the goal rather than guessing; Commitment is engagement genuinely owned, not just verbally agreed, won through involvement rather than pressure; Competence puts the right person on the right task and closes skill gaps; Control is not micromanaging but making progress visible and correctable so drift is caught early. Miss any one and the plan stays on paper — it is a common lens for diagnosing 'why a settled plan fails to get executed'.

oneLiner: 行为由后果决定：被奖励的会重复、被惩罚或忽视的会消退——别谈态度，改后果。
oneLinerEn: Behaviour is shaped by its consequences — what is rewarded recurs, what is punished or ignored fades; change the consequences, not the attitude.
detail: 斯金纳的操作性条件反射被搬到管理：员工的重复行为主要由“之后发生了什么”决定，正强化(及时、具体的表扬与回报)增加行为，负强化(撤掉不快的刺激)也增加行为，惩罚压制行为，消退(不再回应)让其自然减少。它强调即时、明确、可预期，且“抓好的”比“抓错的”更有效；与只讲内在动机的自我决定理论互补——外在胡萝卜对简单可量化的行为立竿见影，对复杂、需要创造与真诚的工作则要慎用，否则易被刷指标、伤内在动机。
detailEn: Skinner's operant conditioning brought into management: repeat behaviour is driven mainly by 'what happened next' — positive reinforcement (timely, specific praise and reward) increases it, negative reinforcement (removing something unpleasant) also increases it, punishment suppresses it, and extinction (withdrawing response) lets it fade. It stresses immediacy, clarity and predictability and that 'catching people doing well' beats 'catching them doing wrong'; it complements self-determination theory, which leans on intrinsic motive — external carrots work fast on simple, measurable behaviour but must be used sparingly on complex, creative, heartfelt work, lest they game the metric and crowd out intrinsic drive.

oneLiner: 从管理自我到管理他人、再管管理者、管职能、管事业部、管集团——每上一级都要换一套工作与心法。
oneLinerEn: From managing self to others, then managers, a function, a division, the enterprise — each rung demands new work and a new mindset, not just a bigger title.
detail: 拉姆·查兰等提出，领导力的成长是六次“转型”而非单纯升职：管理自我、管理他人(放下亲手做、改通过别人拿结果)、管理管理者(不再亲自带一线、去选带管理者)、管理职能(跳出单一部门做跨职能权衡)、管理业务(兼顾短期与长期、面向外部利益相关者)、管理全集团(定战略与文化、面向资本市场)。它解释了很多“提拔即失败”：岗位变了，人却仍用上一层的活法干，于是各层级都退回做各自旧工作，组织空转。真正的晋升要求工作理念、时间与技能的三重转变。
detailEn: Charan and colleagues cast leadership growth as six transitions rather than mere promotions — managing self, managing others (letting go of hands-on work to get results through people), managing managers (leading leaders instead of the front line), managing a function (cross-functional trade-offs beyond one silo), managing a business (balancing short and long term and outside stakeholders) and managing the enterprise (setting strategy and culture for the markets). It explains many 'promoted-to-failure' cases: the seat changes but the person still works one rung down, so every level does its predecessor's job and the organisation spins idle. Real advancement needs a threefold shift in work values, time application and skills.

oneLiner: 以自知、守底线、表里如一赢得信任:领导者的“真”本身就是影响力。
oneLinerEn: Win trust through self-awareness, a moral core and walking your talk — a leader's realness is itself influence.
detail: 在安然、金融危机等“伪善领导”失信之后,管理学转向研究真诚的领导者。真实型领导四要素:自我觉察(懂自己的强项与盲点)、内化道德观(决策忠于价值观而非迎合外部压力)、平衡地处理信息(先倾听征求再下判断)、关系透明(对下属坦诚、也敢于示弱)。它建立在心理安全感之上,通过言行一致积累“信任账户”,带出高承诺的团队,与仆人式、变革型领导互补。
detailEn: After Enron and the financial crisis eroded trust in inauthentic leaders, the field turned to genuine ones. Authentic leadership has four parts: self-awareness (knowing your strengths and blind spots), an internalised moral perspective (choices true to values, not pleasing outside pressure), balanced processing (hearing and weighing before judging) and relational transparency (candid with followers, willing to show weakness). Built on psychological safety, it accrues a trust account through say-do consistency and yields highly committed teams, complementing servant and transformational leadership.

oneLiner: 除经济、人力、社会资本外,还有一种可开发的“心理资本”:希望、效能、韧性、乐观。
oneLinerEn: Besides economic, human and social capital lies a developable psychological capital — Hope, Efficacy, Resilience, Optimism.
detail: 卢桑斯提出的心理资本用首字拼成 HERO:希望(有目标、有路径、有动力)、自我效能(相信自己能成)、韧性(受挫后反弹)、乐观(把成败作暂时且可改变的解释)。与前三种资本不同,它可以被培养和测量,研究显示高水平心理资本与更高绩效、满意度、留任相关。它给管理者一个抓手:别只投技能培训,也要投资员工的信心、复原力与解释风格。
detailEn: Luthans's psychological capital spells out HERO: hope (goals, pathways and the will to pursue them), self-efficacy (belief you can succeed), resilience (bouncing back after setbacks) and optimism (explaining wins and losses as temporary and changeable). Unlike the other three capitals, it can be developed and measured; high PsyCap correlates with better performance, satisfaction and retention. It hands managers a lever: invest not only in skills but in employees' confidence, recovery and explanatory style.

oneLiner: 好目标该具体、可衡量、能达成、相关、有时限——否则只是句口号。
oneLinerEn: A good goal is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound — else it is just a slogan.
detail: SMART 是把笼统愿望变成可执行目标的检验清单:Specific 说清到底做什么、Measurable 定下可量化的标准、Achievable 既有挑战又够得着、Relevant 与更大的目标相关、Time-bound 设明确期限。它常被归于乔治·多里奥特等实践者,与洛克“目标设定理论”(具体而困难的目标更能带动绩效)一脉相承,也常用来给 OKR 的关键结果与 KPI 把关。它是把“想做某事”翻译成“怎样才算做成”的通用语法。
detailEn: SMART is a checklist that turns a vague wish into an executable goal — Specific (what exactly), Measurable (the quantified bar), Achievable (stretching yet reachable), Relevant (tied to a larger aim) and Time-bound (a clear deadline). Often credited to Doriot and other practitioners, it rhymes with Locke's goal-setting theory (specific, hard goals drive performance) and is used to vet OKR key results and KPIs. It is the common grammar for translating I want to do X into what counts as done.

oneLiner: 有些难题没有现成答案：领导要分清技术性问题与适应性挑战，后者得带着大家共同学习，而非替他们作答。
oneLinerEn: Some problems have no ready answer: leaders must tell a technical fix from an adaptive challenge, and for the latter mobilise people to learn, not hand them a solution.
detail: 哈佛学者赫菲提出：技术性问题可由现有能力与权威直接解决，适应性挑战则牵涉价值观、习惯与关系的改变，只能靠集体共同摸索。领导者的功课是先把二者分清、再把问题返还给真正该承担它的当事人，在放任与高压之间维持一个有生产力的调节区间，容忍分歧、保护少数意见，让系统在不至于崩溃的压力下完成学习与改变。它像医生先诊断再决定是否需要手术，与变革型领导互补，专治那些没人握有现成答案的真难题。
detailEn: Harvard's Heifetz distinguished technical problems, solvable with existing know-how and authority, from adaptive challenges that demand change in values, habits and relationships and can only be worked out collectively. The leader's job is to tell the two apart, return the problem to those who actually own it, hold a productive zone between neglect and pressure, tolerate dissent and protect minority voices, so the system learns and changes under stress that does not break it. Like a physician who diagnoses before cutting, it complements transformational leadership and targets the hard problems no one holds a ready answer for.

oneLiner: 领导不必集中于一个人：它是团队轮流承担的共同职能，谁在关键时刻最合适，谁就接过方向盘。
oneLinerEn: Leadership need not sit with one person: it is a shared team function, and whoever fits best at a given moment takes the wheel.
detail: 与伟人式的单点领导相对，分布式领导把影响力看作可在成员间流动、轮流担当的能力。在专业互补、环境多变的团队里，把决策临时交给最懂那块的人，往往比事事上报更快更好。它依赖心理安全感、清晰的共同目标与彼此的补位意愿，也考验在位者肯不肯放权、后进者敢不敢接棒。它不取消负责人，而是把领导从一个人的头衔变成一套团队的协作方式。
detailEn: Set against the great-person view of leadership as one seat, shared leadership treats influence as a capability that flows among members and is taken up in turn. Where skills complement and conditions shift, handing the call to whoever knows that piece best often beats routing everything up the chain. It leans on psychological safety, a clear common purpose and a willingness to cover for one another, and tests whether the incumbent will let go and the next will step up. It does not abolish the lead role but turns leadership from one person's title into the team's way of working.

oneLiner: 领导者的行事方式本身就是最强信号：守规则、担责任、经得起公开审视，才立得起信任与风气。
oneLinerEn: How a leader behaves is itself the loudest signal: keeping to rules, owning responsibility and withstanding public scrutiny is what builds trust and tone.
detail: 伦理型领导关注领导者以公正、诚实、关怀的方式决策，并以自身行为示范组织倡导的价值。研究显示上行下效——主管的操守直接塑造团队的心理安全与道德氛围，影响员工是否敢说真话、会不会随大流失守底线。它包含在人前的公开诚信与在人后的一致操守，也要求在利益冲突、绩效考核、奖惩分配中给出可辩护的判断。它并非软性装饰，而是长期信任与合规的根，一旦塌陷，再好的战略也会被伪善侵蚀。
detailEn: Ethical leadership concerns deciding with fairness, honesty and care, and embodying the values a firm professes through one's own conduct. Research shows the tone flows downward: a manager's integrity shapes the team's psychological safety and moral climate, whether people dare speak truth and whether they slip with the crowd. It covers public probity before others and consistent probity behind them, and demands defensible judgement amid conflicts of interest, appraisals and rewards. Far from soft decoration, it is the root of lasting trust and compliance; once it collapses, even a good strategy is eaten by hypocrisy.

oneLiner: 主动经营与上级的协作：摸清其目标、压力与偏好，定期对齐、带着方案而非只带问题，让授权更顺。
oneLinerEn: Actively run the relationship with your boss: read their goals, pressures and style, align often, bring options not just problems, and make delegating easier.
detail: 向上管理不是逢迎操纵，而是把上下级协作当成一段需要主动经营的工作关系：理解上司真正被考核什么、最怕什么、惯于怎样接收信息，据此调整沟通的节奏与颗粒度；主动同步进展与风险、让坏消息早到而不突然、决策时提供带取舍的备选而非甩锅。它降低上级的不确定感、赢得更宽的授权与更多资源，也替上司分担带宽。边界在于诚信与共同目标——用于把事情办成，而非用于钻营。
detailEn: Managing up is not flattery or manipulation but treating the boss relationship as work you own: understanding what your superior is measured on, fears most and prefers to receive, then matching the cadence and granularity of your communication to it. Share progress and risk proactively, let bad news land early and never as a surprise, and when deciding, bring costed options instead of dumping problems. It lowers your superior's uncertainty, earns wider delegation and more resources, and spares their bandwidth. Its boundary is honesty and a shared goal — used to get things done, not to scheme.
